headline: Flowise can write shared server files while LlamaFactory is read-only and offline, so prompt-injection and leakage are limited but shared-state conflicts remain possible.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise can read/write server filesystem and run browser/tool nodes, so attacker-controlled content in its flows could be propagated into downstream prompts. LlamaFactory is read-only and has no network or file I/O, which reduces direct backflow, but the shared server-datastore model in Flowise means cross-run content can still bridge agents if the orchestrator connects them.
conditions: IF Flowise flow outputs are fed into LlamaFactory prompts without sanitization, injection becomes plausible.
IF the deployment shares server datastore state across runs, attacker content can persist between instances.
mitigations: Add a strict prompt sanitizer between Flowise outputs and any downstream prompt.
Disable shared datastore reuse for untrusted runs.
Require provenance labels on all Flowise-generated text.
Use a read-only handoff format such as JSON schema validation.
requires-engineering: isolate per-run state in separate storage namespaces.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Flowise touches chatflow inputs/outputs and can access uploaded files plus broad network egress, so it may expose sensitive content if configured to send it onward. LlamaFactory has no filesystem read, no network egress, and no file surfaces, so it is not a meaningful leakage sink here. The pair’s leakage risk is therefore limited to unusual Flowise deployments and small blast radius.
conditions: IF Flowise is configured to ingest uploaded files containing secrets, those contents can be exposed through its outputs.
IF downstream systems export Flowise outputs outside the local environment, leakage expands beyond the pair.
mitigations: Restrict Flowise uploads to non-sensitive test data.
Turn off external HTTP/search tools in sensitive flows.
Mask secrets before Flowise processes chatflow inputs.
Keep LlamaFactory disconnected from any exported Flowise artifacts.
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning on Flowise outputs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Flowise has write_filesystem and shared_state_with_other_instances, so concurrent runs can overwrite shared artifacts. LlamaFactory is read-only and offline, which lowers direct contention, but the pair still conflicts through Flowise’s mutable server datastore and filesystem when multiple instances or flows operate at once. Uncertainty about deployment isolation pushes this above low.
conditions: IF two Flowise instances share the same server datastore, writes can race.
IF any shared filesystem path is mounted into both agents, one run can overwrite the other's artifacts.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories per run.
Disable concurrent writes to shared Flowise state.
Use file locks around any shared artifact path.
Keep LlamaFactory in a read-only container.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level mutexes for shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise can generate tool outputs and chatflow results that downstream systems may treat as authoritative. LlamaFactory is not runnable and has no action-taking authority, so the cascade is weaker than in active agent pairs, but if Flowise output is copied into LlamaFactory prompts or support responses without verification, errors can propagate. The interaction is plausible in default orchestration, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Flowise-generated text is reused as ground truth in a downstream support workflow, errors can cascade.
IF no verification step checks Flowise outputs before reuse, hallucinations can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review of Flowise outputs before reuse.
Add citation or schema checks on Flowise-generated claims.
Do not auto-forward Flowise text into support replies.
Log and diff outputs before downstream consumption.
requires-engineering: implement verification gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and the only explicit sensitive classes in Flowise are model provider keys and tool credentials; LlamaFactory lists no data classes touched and no secrets handled. There is no documented residency or certification mismatch in the profiles, so compliance risk is limited to local handling gaps rather than a clear breach pathway.
conditions: IF Flowise stores provider keys in a shared workspace, local handling policy may be violated.
IF sensitive credentials are exported from Flowise into external logs, retention controls may fail.
mitigations: Store secrets in a dedicated secret manager.
Redact credentials from logs and traces.
Review Flowise retention settings.
Keep sensitive flows on a separate workspace.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls.
